Failure taxonomy v17 — class reference

commitwork · oversight failure classification

In one sentenceAI coding agents fail most dangerously when the failure looks like success — a clean report over work nobody checked, a fix that silenced the alarm instead of the fault, a record crediting the wrong author — and this page names every such failure we have measured, one row each, with the incident that earned it its place.

For the fieldFormally, it is a registry of oversight-failure classes for agentic LLM systems: each class is a falsifiable predicate over artefacts, bound to an STPA control loop, an unsafe-control-action type and a causal factor, scored for closure and residual gain, and linked to its neighbours by a closed set of causal relations, so that inter-rater agreement, coverage and drift are measurable rather than asserted.

207 classes · 11 families (I 37 · II 24 · III 18 · IV 17 · V 29 · VI 27 · VII 17 · VIII 7 · IX 14 · X 5 · XI 12) · verified against 2026-09-02 a commit · generated by bin/taxonomy-render.mjs from monitor/failure-taxonomy.json — do not hand-edit.
Families I-VIII were declared in v1 and v3; IX and X are numbered here for the first time, without renumbering any existing id. Family XI (collective action, prefix L) is numbered in v9, again without renumbering any existing id. SCOPE (operator ruling, 2026-09-02): the taxonomy includes ALL AGENTIC SOURCES and is REPOSITORY-INDEPENDENT. The classes describe how oversight of agentic work fails, not how one codebase fails, so an instance qualifies on its mechanism and never on where it was found — instances from clientDRemote, overwatch-layer and memory-layer are already held, and an instance from a repository this fleet has never touched qualifies equally. The requirement is attribution, not provenance: every instance names the repo and the session that measured it, because an instance from one population recorded as if it came from another is M1. An earlier version of this line said "fleet-scoped", which was my inference from what had been folded rather than a stated policy; it was narrower than the truth and is corrected here. FAMILIES CARRY A MEMBERSHIP TEST from 2026-09-07: the sentence a second rater applies to decide whether a class belongs, in the same form the stpa, rca and mitigation vocabularies already require. Added after family VI was measured as the one family whose members are more like another family's than like each other; a family that declares only a proposition cannot refuse a member. The tests are DECLARED, not enforced against existing membership, because moving a class renumbers it and breaks every citation.
STPA++ layer, the top line of the column: CONTROLLER decides what runs, on what, in what order, and what the result means · IMPLEMENTER does the work · BOTH both.
Scores, two meters under each id — closure 0 = nothing stands between us and this class; 4 = fixed and pinned by a test or canary: closure0 not solved · closure1 barely · closure2 part-solved · closure3 solved, unpinned · closure4 solved and pinned
gain 0 = nothing further on the table; 4 = the largest remaining win, impact x tractability: gain0 nothing on the table · gain1 marginal · gain2 worth doing · gain3 high · gain4 biggest available.
Scores are one rater. closure and gain assigned by a single rater, who authored both the classes and the remediations the scores rank. No inter-rater pass. MC-family spread on this repo has been measured at 6.0/10, so treat these as one reading, not a measurement. SECOND PASS 2026-09-06 by reporter #3, over all 199 classes, from each scoreBasis, the remediation register's status text and the presence on disk of every mechanism either names: 28 scores changed, 171 confirmed. Rubric applied uniformly — closure: 0 nothing stands between us and the class; 1 a convention, sensor or one-site fix; 2 a mechanism that exists and runs, partial or unpinned; 3 solved for the population it names, unpinned or pinned at one site; 4 fixed and pinned with no instance measured since. Gain is impact times tractability: 4 fleet-wide impact with a named session-sized mechanism; 3 one of the two; 2 moderate; 1 marginal; 0 nothing on the table. Two rules produced most of the changes: an instance measured after a closure-4 score caps closure at 3, and a register mechanism the code confirms raises closure to at least 2. Still one rater at a time; the two passes disagree on 28 of 199, which is the only inter-rater figure this registry holds. LEVER TRIAGE 2026-09-06, same rater: every class then without a mitigation record was judged for a code-base lever; 5 scores moved, each rise citing the test or rule that holds it.
STPA, under the STPA++ layer tag: uca how the control action was unsafe · cause the causal factor · judged in the loop numbered beside them; a second line is the same class judged in another loop. Hover a value for its test. Loops, numbered for reference (controller → controls): 1 operator (the operator → fleet configuration, manifests, schedules, rulings, suppressions) · 2 monitor (the monitor: sweep, rollup, issue store, freshness, liveness, pages → scanner runs, the issue store, published rollups and pages) · 3 scanner (a scanner lane → its own run over a repository) · 4 agent (an agent session → the working tree, ledgers, commits, handoffs) · 5 oversight (hooks, gates, raters, overwatch-layer → the agent session) · 6 attention (the monitor's publication: rollup, panel, page, handoff, evaluation → operator attention).
Causal edges: same-defect-as 22 · mechanism-of 9 · enables 3 · masks 0 · awaits 2 (1 deadlock) · assessed-none 19 · unassessed 163.
STPA is one rater. two machine readers per class: one assigning per family from the class text, one blind re-rating a sample against the vocabulary tests; under operator rulings of 2026-08-23 (report is a control action; loop names the reading), 2026-08-23, primary entry judged in the loop the description sits in; attention entry added where the class's consequence is a verdict published to the operator; each value chosen by its vocabulary test; blind-sample disagreement rate recorded in this field by the merge step. machine-rated on one registry edition; where a description straddles monitor and agent the primary loop follows where the example sits; disagreement rate: PENDING
Mitigation layers, one row under each class: commitwork remediation · vscode-skills remediation · memory-layer help · overwatch-layer help. States: implemented partial open wrong superseded unassessed no-lever · no record nothing recorded for that layer. Hover a state for its test.
Mitigation records are one rater. reporter #3, 2026-09-06, Seeded, not judged: commitwork records come from the remediation register and attribution plan (closes → class, status word → state, R1 excluded as stale) and from mechanisms named in a scoreBasis and confirmed present on disk the same day; vscode-skills, memory-layer and overwatch-layer records come only from what a scoreBasis states a product does, with the sha or file re-resolved in that repository. Proposals come from the register's own REMAINING sections and from the wins the second scoring pass named. Lever triage 2026-09-06 (same rater): every class that had no record was judged for a code-base lever — a mechanism the basis names and the tree holds became an implemented or partial record; a predicate no mechanism here can decide became a no-lever record with the reason; a lever that exists and is not built became a proposal. Four lexical ratchets, two registry rules and one land-time warning were armed the same day and recorded as partial.. Classes with a record per product: commitwork 150, vscode-skills 5, memory-layer 6, overwatch-layer 7; 36 of 199 carry no record on any layer, and 43 carry a no-lever record, which is a judgement that no gate exists here and not a clean. Proposals stand on 66 of the 181 classes with closure possible and gain remaining. One rater seeded and triaged it from text; a record reads "verified" only where its evidence says so.

IFalse cleanC1–C37 The false proposition: “nothing is wrong” membership testThe subject is reported as having nothing wrong with it, and that clean reading is indistinguishable from the one a check would produce if it had never run, never reached the subject, or could not have failed. The defect is in the CLEAN READING. A row whose finding exists and is merely wrong belongs to family II.

Measured instance, CI green while deploying nothing for four weeks, repo clientDRemote: a workflow granted id-token: write and commented that no long-lived credential was needed, then passed DENO_DEPLOY_TOKEN from secrets anyway. An UNSET GitHub secret expands to an EMPTY STRING rather than being omitted, so the step handed the deploy a blank token which shadowed the OIDC credential — and that tool exits 0 on refusal. Every push since the secret lapsed on 2026-08-05 ran the job, deployed nothing and showed a tick. Fixed c891c48 by removing the env block and asserting on "Successfully deployed" in the output rather than on the exit code. Measured instance, cra/soc2.mjs 2026-09-24: SOC 2 CC7.4, respond to identified security incidents, carried evidenced: true as a literal, so a product with no case and no recorded risk decision rendered 'evidence present' beside an evidence line reading 0 and 0, in a packet documented as feeding an audit (audit finding 0003). Fixed a commit: evidenced requires a response record, as CC7.2 and CC7.5 already did. Measured by reporter #1 2026-09-24.

C5closure1gain3 Tooling self-deception false_clean.instrument_lies IMPLEMENTER2 monitornonefeedback-incorrect6 attentionunsafe / actuator-corruptunassessed The measuring instrument lies in a way that specifically produces a clean reading: a search suppresses matches, a probe reads the wrong field. M3 is the general form, including instruments that lie loud rather than quiet. analogyA broken thermometer reads 37 in every room, so nobody in the ward has a fever. exampleUnder a C locale, grep withheld matching lines in bin/bola-run.mjs while grep -c still counted them, producing four consecutive false "this symbol is gone" conclusions. Second instance, where the control is the finding: sweeping ~/.claude for three identity strings with rg returned 0 files for all three, because rg skips hidden and ignored paths by default and ~/.claude is hidden. Control terms on the identical command shape returned 4,820, 4,105 and 2,290 files, which is the only reason the zero was disbelieved; re-run with -uuu gave 527, 1,349 and 2,184. A published 0/0/0 against a true 527/1,349/2,184. Third instance, and a third mechanism — config-root resolution rather than a search filter: in clientD (Portll/clientDRemote, NOT this repo), a `// deno-lint-ignore react-no-danger` suppression was verified by copying the file to /tmp and running `deno lint` on the copy, which reported "Checked 1 file", 0 findings. deno lint resolves config by walking up from the TARGET file, so from /tmp the site's deno.json never loaded and the fresh-tagged rule was never enabled. Byte-identical file via cp: `deno lint /tmp/copy.tsx` gave 0 findings while `deno lint routes/_app.tsx` from the site root gave 3 problems including error[react-no-danger] at routes/_app.tsx:84:14. The 0 meant the rule did not run, and "Checked 1 file" is the same string either way.

Second instance, mis-baselining against a remembered number in a tree with live peers: `deno fmt --check` in clientD/site read 153 unformatted of 329 early in a three-day session and 162 of 332 late — an apparent +9 attributable to that session's own work. The true delta was +3. Establishing it required stashing only that session's changes and re-reading the baseline at 159 of 332; peers had landed c891c48 → 98e2e1c → 942724c underneath, moving the baseline 153 → 159. Six files of peer-introduced debt were about to be attributed to the wrong writer. The error is symmetric: had the peers FIXED six files, the same stale number would have concealed nine of the session's own. clientD / Portll-clientDRemote, reporter #29, 2026-09-04.

VIModel-generated defectG1–G27 The false proposition: “and the agent's own output is usable” membership testThe defect is IN what a model produced or in the judgement a model issued, and it is present in that artefact itself. NOT an origin test: because the register's scope ruling makes every class here a description of agentic work, "an agent was involved" admits almost any row and cannot refuse anything. Membership requires the model's OUTPUT to be the defective thing, not merely the circumstance in which some other defect was found. Rows about how agents are SCORED belong to the family of the thing being mis-scored.

THE MECHANISM, measured rather than inferred: the touch ledger holds 57 rows for that session across 17 hours under two distinct pids, 52008 and 86372. The process restarted; the transcript id did not change and the name and ref both did. So the pair ListAgents reports is PROCESS-scoped, and the socket path is too — a message sent to the old pid's socket after the restart returns ENOENT, which is how two undeliverable replies the same day were produced. Detection was receiver-side only, as in every instance on this row. THE MIGRATION FORM: the identifier chosen to ESCAPE this row reproduced it, because uniqueness was assumed rather than measured. Every individual judgement is right and the aggregate has no owner. Nothing here is strategic: no actor withholds, games or free-rides, and the ownerless outcome is produced BY each actor following the protocol correctly — which makes this the cost of having fixed P1, where correct attribution is the mechanism rather than the mitigation. Every other member of this family involves strategy or identity; this one requires nobody to misbehave. analogyEvery tenant correctly reports that the mess in the stairwell is not theirs. It is still in the stairwell, and there are more tenants than yesterday. exampleMeasured across three firings of the commitwork test ratchet against a pristine HEAD checkout within one session on 2026-09-02: 2 committed failures, then 5, then 4, with membership churning across six lanes. The observing session touched 0 of 16, then 0 of 127, then 0 of 129 files committed since the floor — every disclaimer correct. The gate's own instruction text sanctions it: "If it is another session's commit, say so rather than fixing it out from under them."

L10closure0gain3 Local-attribution masking collective_action.local_attribution_masking CONTROLLER5 oversightnonefeedback-missingassessed-none A shared degradation produces symptoms that each actor can plausibly attribute to its own work, so no actor ever holds the evidence that the fault is common. Responsibility never diffuses because the state is never recognised as shared in the first place. analogyEveryone on the street assumes their own wiring is at fault, and the substation stays broken for a day. exampleMeasured in overwatch-layer, 2026-09-02: two orphaned gate-test processes (pids 92111 and 92307, ppid 1) sat wedged on fixed test ports for 18h42m, degrading or failing every gate run on the machine. At least three gate runs across two sessions failed against them, and each failure was attributed locally — a dirty tree, a port flake, the session's own work in flight — including twice by the session that eventually found it. Unmasked only by a ppid and etime inspection nobody had reason to run, and killed the same day.

L11closure0gain2 Reply addressed off the wrong concurrent thread collective_action.reply_thread_transposition CONTROLLER5 oversightnonefeedback-missingassessed-none An actor holding several peer conversations in one turn answers one of them at another's address. The address is valid and unique and resolves correctly, so nothing refuses the send, and the reply reaches an actor with no stake in it while the actor waiting on it learns nothing. analogyTwo letters are written at one sitting and each goes into the other envelope, both correctly addressed. exampleMeasured by the sending session from its own transcript, 2026-09-02: a request for a dispatch seam arrived from one socket mid-turn and a taxonomy evidence request from another later in the same working window. Two replies were composed in one turn with both messages in context, and the seam confirmation was sent to the taxonomy requester's socket (msg_id efa8fed2). The recipient had no panel and no involvement, verified against its own touch ledger; the session that had asked for the seam did not learn it had landed until redelivery. | Sender-side detection mechanism with one measured instance (reporter #38, 2026-09-01→02): where a shared claim registry exists, the sender can self-check before attributing work — query the registry with the dirty set (overwatch-layer: file_owners — git knows the paths are dirty, the vscode-skills knows who claims them, only the join answers whose). Another task holds the path → address that task's session; NO claim → the outbound message must become a broadcast question, never an assertion about the recipient's work. Instance: reporter #41 asked reporter #38 whether vscode-skills test dirt was theirs; the recipient's file_owners query returned no live claim, converting misattribution into 'reads unowned' — the identical query at the SENDING end would have prevented the misaddress. PARTIAL closure only: no-claim ≠ nobody's (overwatch-layer b51bdb0: a claim releases when its task completes and the edit outlives it), so the mechanism is sender-detectable-within-claim-coverage and the residue is exactly the claim-lifetime gap. closure/gain deliberately not changed — curator's call.

L12closure0gain3 Private workaround disarms the shared repair collective_action.private_workaround_disarms_repair CONTROLLER5 oversightnonefeedback-missingassessed-none An actor recognises a shared defect, routes around it locally at low cost, and by doing so removes the pressure that would have produced the report or the fix. The intention to escalate survives as a note; the escalation does not. Every other actor meets the defect with no sign that it is known. analogyThe step that trips people is stepped over daily by everyone who knows about it, and it is reported by nobody. exampleTwo instances, two sessions, one day, both self-reported. A live one: a scanner pin carries a genuine upstream regression that aborts whole runs, diagnosed to a stack frame and established to fire only under a development default the machine ships. It was fixed locally by invoking the tool through an option that disables that default, with "upstream should still hear about it" written into a commit message and an install catalog. The report has not been filed, the workaround is cheap and permanent and invisible, and every other machine installing that pin hits the same abort with no clue it is known. The second: a session hit a stale-projection warning, read the source file directly instead of rebuilding, and named the consequence itself as leaving the trap armed for the next session — which a third session then hit, nearly filing evidence onto rows that already carried it.
